newly_rule: Trends first seen on Google's free Trending-now RSS with fewer than 2 observations and no second source: listed with what is unknown, not ranked yet. They join Search Trends' ranking at stage Building.
score_rule: Score 0–100 = 40 × Google + 25 × Wikipedia + 20 × timing + 15 × Airtel fit. Google = heat ÷ 100 (Search Trends: the row's own newest observation set, heat-v2). Wikipedia = ½ × min(1, log10(reads 7d) ÷ 5.5) + ½ × min(1, rise 7d ÷ 200%). Timing = live / match today 1 · new on platform ≤ 7 d 0.7 · match tomorrow 0.6 · else 0. Airtel fit = ₹99 card 1 · ₹279 pack 0.8 · ₹149 pack 0.6 · Prime plans 0.4 · free app 0.3 · not via Airtel 0 (never listed). Candidates: Search Trends 'Promote now' · Title Attention by Platform risers (≥ +50% 7d, ≥ 10K reads) · Wikipedia Attention movers (Indian-language reads ≥ +100% 7d and ≥ 10K in 7 days — the rise and the reads on one basis; with an Airtel platform; a person only through the match his current Search Trends row links him to) · India matches today / tomorrow on an Airtel app, until the match has ended. One row per thing: a match's spellings and its players fold into the match (fixture pair) — a folded player lends his Google signal, never his platform, Wikidata id, link or Wikipedia reads; titles merge on Wikidata id. Route (Airtel fit): the fixture calendar › the thing's own trend / platform row › its reading row — never the best fit on offer. Match names as the fixture calendar writes them. At most 5 of 8 from one lane. Confidence: high = ≥ 2 independent signals agree; else the signal's own confidence.

changes.rule: Google: the latest scan vs yesterday's last scan (heat change; NEW = on neither list yesterday, incl. trends that reached Google's RSS lists after the scan). Wikipedia: the newest day vs the day before (reading page and platform titles with a daily curve; the day before ≥ 500 reads). Up to 3 new, 3 risers, 2 fallers; one row per thing. A heat measured differently (growth scored in one scan only, or a different set of state feeds answering) is shown as 'Different measurement', never with an arrow. Each Google row names its read (scan HH:MM or RSS HH:MM).
